title: Jean du Bellay (London) to Montmorency, 1528-29, BnF fr. 3077 and fr. 3078 (catalogue item 4)

plaintext.source: Not in Le Grand 1688, L&P or Bourrilly 1905; Scheurer 1969 not checked

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF btv1b9060311s, p. 21 at full size (p21_transcription.md)
transcription.notes: Eight cipher lines, about 190 signs (NOTES estimate); glyph reading at 4,262 px is the limit.

plaintext.source: Court decipherer's word-by-word interlinear; Le Grand, Histoire du divorce III (1688) pp. 327-332

transcription.notes: Used only to align signs with the interlinear reading to re-derive the key.

plaintext.source: Le Grand III pp. 369-375, from a deciphered copy (Clair. 330 f. 71)

transcription.notes: Only the first cipher lines of p. 113 read sign by sign, as an independent check.

system.summary: 'Bayonne's cipher' of 1529: homophonic symbol alphabet with 2-5 signs per letter, a few nulls and word signs (roy, madame, bien, fault, paix, le Cardinal).
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's table of Bayonne's cipher (from Clair. 333, June 1530) and Friedmann's reconstruction (NAF 4206, not seen); Tomokiyo's table used and extended.
system.notes: No k/v/w; u = v. Max homophones from the NOTES table (a has five signs, s and u/v four). unread_groups = three signs on p. 21 not seen on pp. 25-27. key_order 'random' is inferred from the sign table, not stated in NOTES.

prior_solution.where: Le Grand 1688 (four 1529 letters), Bourrilly and de Vaissière 1905 (28 Oct 1528); 16 June 1529 not in print

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Gallica IIIF for fr. 3077/3078; connections dropped and 429s, only fr. 3078 pp. 21-27, 31-32 (later 113-117, 133-134) at full size.
Dated the notice items against Le Grand 1688, L&P IV and Bourrilly 1905: all five catalogue letters are in print in clear.
Re-derived the key from the 22 June letter's interlinear decipherment, extending Tomokiyo's table (B = o, word signs bien, fault, paix).
Read the 16 June 1529 block (p. 21) in stretches, about 60 % of signs.
Key read the opening of the 17 Oct letter from the leaf, matching Le Grand; boxed cross = le Cardinal.

outcome.method_basis: All five letters of the catalogue item are printed in clear from the Court's decipherments (Le Grand 1688; Bourrilly and de Vaissiere 1905 for 28 Oct 1528); the project also re-derived Tomokiyo's 'Bayonne's cipher' table from the 22 June 1529 interlinear decipherment in the same volume (fr. 3078 pp. 25-27) and used it to read about 60% of the unprinted 16 June 1529 block.
outcome.notes: Catalogue item closed as found already solved; the by-product 16 June 1529 block is read in part (about 60 % of signs, NOTES estimate); Scheurer 1969 unchecked.
